story: At 12:17 on a sunny Wednesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is squinting at the street bulletin board on Magnolia Loop, hunting for the Architectural Review form before he wires up another string of lights. Donna, looking a little sheepish, is thinning her pink flamingo flock down to three out front to comply with rule L-02, and Hal, gruff but cooperative, has told Gary to file at Town Hall first and taken Donna's word that three flamingos will square things. Meanwhile, over at Rosa's House, Rosa is determinedly penciling in a shopping window between her shifts so Saturday stays clear.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Look over the board for an Architectural Review form or filing instructions
Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos and leave just three out front to comply with L-02
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Pick a shopping window between shifts and double-check Saturday is fully clear

gary.thought_process: Donna and Hal are busy with the flamingo business, and I already told Donna tomorrow morning works. I asked about the blank Architectural Review forms and nobody answered, but the street bulletin board is right here and might have them posted. If I can find the form, I can file it and get back to the cart wiring. No point standing around while they sort out ornaments.

parameters.content: Look over the board for an Architectural Review form or filing instructions

donna.thought_process: Gary said yes to tomorrow morning at the rec center, so my Saturday-ish plan is moving and I shouldn't ask him again. Hal is right, though: I'm well over the three-ornament limit, and I told him I'd trim the flock. Better to actually do it than keep chatting and earn a notice. I'm standing on Magnolia Loop with the flamingo flock right here, so I'll pull the extras and leave three.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos and leave just three out front to comply with L-02

hal.thought_process: Donna has agreed to trim the flamingos to three, so there's no violation to write up. Pressing her again would just be nagging. Gary asked where the Architectural Review blanks are, and I know the committee's paperwork better than anyone on this street. His cart mod does need sign-off, and helping him file it properly is the by-the-book answer. It also fits my reflection about being a neighbor, not just a scorekeeper.

parameters.content: Gary, the Architectural Review blanks are at Town Hall. File before you wire another inch, and I'll quit asking. And Donna, I'll take your word on the flamingos. Three, and we're square.

rosa.thought_process: I've planned the menu, locked the seating, and finalized the grocery list, and Hal has already said yes. Nobody is around to talk to. Gary and Donna haven't answered my invitation yet, and Donna is the one I haven't actually asked directly. Rather than re-planning, I should block out when I'm shopping against my shifts. The shift schedule is right here, so I'll pin down the shopping window and make sure Saturday is clear.

parameters.content: Pick a shopping window between shifts and double-check Saturday is fully clear

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
